title: Who May See This Record?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Judge whether each of eight requests to see or use a student's learning record should be allowed, allowed only with an agreement and family notice, or refused.

learningObjectives: The learner will judge whether each of eight requests to see or use a student's learning record should be allowed, allowed only with an agreement and family notice, or not allowed, correctly judging at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Learning record, student-controlled data and its five parts, and data portability, from the section "Data Portability and Student-Controlled Data" in Chapter 8.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Judge concrete requests against stated principles, with feedback on each case
keyQuestions: Who is asking, and do they have an educational need?
Is the purpose within what the family was told?
commonMisconceptions: Anyone at the school may see any student's record
A vendor may use records for any purpose once it has them
A family may only look at the record, never take a copy
assessmentOpportunities: A teacher views her own class's mastery records to plan. Response?
The vendor wants identifiable records to train a new commercial product. Response?
A district-approved tutoring partner asks for one student's fractions mastery. Response?
May a family take a copy of the record?

controls.name: Allow, Agreement and family notice, Do not allow
Submit
controls.description: commits it. Two attempts per request; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves on; after the eighth it shows your score.

controls.name: Show the responses and principles
controls.description: checkbox that shows what each response means and the five principles.

controls.name: Try again
controls.description: reshuffles the requests and starts over.
